overall: Resolved by informal action: the Commission violated the OML by three members' late certifications, but the AG found no intentional violation, no penalty, and ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Three members allegedly did not certify receipt of Open Meeting Law materials within two weeks of appointment, as the law requires.
allegations.key_passage: we find, that the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law when three members did not complete and sign certification attesting to their receipt of Open Meeting Law materials

allegations.summary: The Commission urged the AG to decline review of the complaint as untimely, raised for the first time in a supplemental response.
allegations.key_passage: As this argument was not made in the original response, we do not consider it.

allegations.summary: The complainant asked that each of the three members be fined and called the late certifications fraudulent and egregious.
allegations.key_passage: The Law does not provide for civil penalties against individual members of a public body.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Commission’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
